claims.claim_en: Other EU states lack BEHG-comparable CO2 pricing except Austria, creating a German competitive disadvantage.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: Swedish government carbon tax, non-ETS industry full rate since 2018
Official natural gas carbon-tax rates applicable before 14 October 2026

claims.explanation: Sweden and Ireland provide primary examples of carbon pricing outside ETS1. However, comparable may mean a BEHG-style national trading instrument or the burden on particular chemical processes; coverage, exemptions and effective burdens were not matched.
claims.limits: Do not turn the existence of a carbon tax into proof of identical BEHG burdens or deny relative competitiveness effects without matched firms/processes.

claims.claim_en: Many VCI member companies receive at most half of actual nEHS cost through BECV, with counter-performance obligations.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: §§7–11: intensity, benchmarks, deductible, compensation and counter-performance

claims.explanation: The formula can produce less than half of actual costs despite nominal sector percentages, and counter-performance duties exist. No representative member-company cost/payment data were obtained for many.
claims.limits: A nominal 65–95% compensation factor does not refute the effective-cost claim; eligibility and benchmark adjustments matter.

claims.claim_en: BECV intensity divides eligible nEHS emissions by the company’s full gross value added, excluding ETS1 emissions from the numerator.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: The full-company gross-value-added definition and §9 exclusion of ETS1 fuel emissions confirm the formula.
claims.limits: Autonomous company-part treatment under §6 can change the organisational perimeter; the claim describes the company calculation.

claims.claim_en: Adding ETS1 activity and its gross value added can reduce measured nEHS intensity and compensation eligibility.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: Holding nEHS emissions fixed, adding positive gross value added lowers the ratio and can affect the threshold. This validates the conditional mechanical premise.
claims.limits: It does not show all mixed companies receive lower aid than an otherwise appropriate comparator, or establish unfairness.

claims.claim_en: Separately measuring ETS1 installation gross value added is practically impossible.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: The law does not require the proposed installation split, but that does not prove it is practically impossible in every relevant company. Accounts and firm-level feasibility evidence were not available.
claims.limits: No universal feasibility or impossibility conclusion is admitted.

claims.claim_en: BECV heat and fuel benchmarks are taken from ETS1.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: The regulation directly links to ETS1 heat/fuel benchmark values.
claims.limits: Suitability or methodological weakness is a policy/technical evaluation beyond this narrow source identity.

claims.original_excerpt: erfasst auch Anlagen aus anderen EU-
claims.claim_en: The ETS benchmarks are based on installations in other EU states as well as Germany.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: §2 and §9 links to EU-wide benchmark regulation

claims.explanation: The referenced benchmark framework is EU-wide rather than a German-only reference population.
claims.limits: The claim does not itself quantify whether the resulting benchmark disadvantages German firms.

claims.claim_en: Natural gas is the principal fuel for the predominant part of German industry.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: 14 November 2025 industrial energy use: natural gas 29.2%, largest energy source

claims.explanation: Primary aggregate energy statistics establish gas as the largest energy source, but not that it is the principal fuel for a majority of firms, installations, subsectors or output.
claims.limits: The denominator of predominant part is unspecified; aggregate share cannot silently replace it.

claims.claim_en: The draft raises overflow price from €68 to €73 and top-up price from €70 to €75.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: Prices refer to the 2026 and 2027 certificate vintages. Top-ups for those vintages occur in 2027 and 2028 respectively.
claims.limits: The author uses vintage-year shorthand, not proof the 2026 top-up was sold during calendar 2026.

claims.claim_en: 2026 auctions absorbed the offered certificates and cleared at the corridor ceiling.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: Final annual budget and €65 double-volume mechanism

claims.explanation: Every reported clearing price is €65; allocations total 192,084,807 against 192,085,240 planned, a residual of 433 (0.00023%). This supports ordinary rounded language of essentially full take-up.
claims.limits: Current CSV was retrieved later but each row is dated before the statement; a minute rounding residue is not material.

claims.claim_en: Every auction participant received only a fraction of its bid volume.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: Bids versus allocations and successful bidder counts

claims.explanation: Aggregate oversubscription is extreme and pro-rata allocation supports rationing at the marginal price. But confidential individual bid prices/quantities are unavailable; some participants were unsuccessful, and the literal every participant statement cannot be reconstructed.
claims.limits: Zero allocations and multi-price bid curves complicate a universal formulation; no material error is inferred from this shorthand.

claims.claim_en: The Commission proposes municipal-waste incineration phase-in over 2031–2034 and excludes hazardous-waste incineration.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: Primary EUR-Lex search extraction COM(2026)616, explanatory memorandum and recitals 73–74

claims.explanation: The original proposal indexed by the official legislative publisher specifies that timetable and hazardous-waste exclusion.
claims.limits: Proposal, not enacted final future coverage; optional derogations and capacity thresholds mean the timetable is a general phase-in, not every plant simultaneously.

claims.claim_en: Hazardous and municipal waste used as fuel are expressly excluded from ETS2.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: The primary Directive text excludes release for consumption of hazardous or municipal waste used as fuel.
claims.limits: The author’s general waste-fuel shorthand is read in the hazardous/municipal waste-incineration context, not all materials legally classified as waste.

claims.claim_en: Hazardous waste that cannot be avoided or recycled must be energetically recovered under BImSchG, permits and KrWG.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: §§6–8 and 15: hierarchy, recovery conditions and disposal

claims.explanation: The general statutes retain disposal where recovery is technically impossible or unreasonable, so they do not establish an unconditional universal recovery rule. Context expressly mentions sufficient heating value and plant permits, which might narrow the intended claim.
claims.limits: Specific permits and waste streams were not inspected; the contextual qualifier prevents admission of an overstatement solely from the general statutory exception.

claims.claim_en: Hazardous incineration accounts for 1.33 million tonnes, approximately 2.8% of the thermally treated waste in the cited study.
claims.policy_link: Industrial cost compensation, auctions and waste exclusions
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check

evidence.locator: Physical page 7, figure 2.1, visually inspected: 2019 quantities 1.33 and 46.77 million tonnes

claims.explanation: 1.33/46.77×100 = 2.84%, matching 2.8% rounded. The source figure is a waste-mass denominator, not CO2 emissions or fiscal revenue.
claims.limits: 2019 statistics reproduced in a March 2022 report; excludes waste treated solely in firms’ own facilities. Not a measured 2026 share.

claims.claim_en: The proposal reduces the per-auction maximum bid from 50% to 20%.
claims.policy_link: Procurement rules and cost of compliance
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: The before/after statutory percentages match, with the new rule applying to 2027 compliance buyers.
claims.limits: Evidence evaluated as of the authored October 2026 statement; later snapshots do not by themselves prove historical applicability.

claims.claim_en: Reducing the bid cap redistributes the auction volume rather than creating additional certificates.
claims.policy_link: Procurement rules and cost of compliance
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: Changing the individual limit leaves the total auction budget formula distinct. This narrow mechanism does not imply no overflow certificates are available.
claims.limits: The wider rhetorical claim of systemic scarcity must be distinguished from finite cheap-auction capacity and unlimited premium sale.

claims.claim_en: Demand for the 2026 auctions exceeded the offered auction volume.
claims.policy_link: Procurement rules and cost of compliance
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: All reported auction bid volumes greatly exceed allocations, even after double-volume sales at the upper corridor price.
claims.limits: Bids are not unique annual compliance demand and may include repeated need or strategic quantities; do not sum bids across auctions as unique demand.

claims.claim_en: A lower bid ceiling can require a high-need buyer to spread a given procurement volume across more auctions.
claims.policy_link: Procurement rules and cost of compliance
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: With auction volume A and fixed requirement N, the minimum rounds permitted by the cap changes from ceiling(N/0.5 A) to ceiling(N/0.2 A).
claims.limits: Conditional arithmetic; realised allocation and secondary purchasing can differ. It does not establish universal risk or pass-through magnitude.

claims.claim_en: Higher overflow/top-up prices inevitably increase risk premiums and are passed through to end customers.
claims.policy_link: Procurement rules and cost of compliance
claims.check_method: Full original context, independent primary evidence, temporal applicability and definitions check
claims.explanation: The draft changes marginal procurement costs, but pass-through and premia depend on contracts, hedging, market power and the share of certificates bought at premium prices. No transaction or contract evidence establishes inevitability.
claims.limits: A conditional risk mechanism is plausible; no quantitative or universal causal effect is accepted.

claims.claim_en: Both premium certificate prices increase by €5 for the 2027 vintage.
claims.policy_link: Procurement rules and cost of compliance

evidence.locator: Physical pages2–3, table1 and counterfactual discussion

claims.claim_en: Under the 2027 draft, firms receive roughly€21.7 billion and households€11.7 billion in KTF programme allocation.

evidence.locator: Figures/tables on sector allocations; method physical pages12–13

General endorsement of carbon pricing effectiveness and criticism of weakened incentives are economic/policy judgments without a defined measurable effect. Proposed transition conditions and funding guarantees are preferences. Testable statutory and sectoral premises inventoried.

Fair-market recommendations,  KTF purpose judgments and targeted climate dividend proposals are normative; possible future use of EU Social Climate Fund is expressly conditional,  not a claim of present eligibility for a specific instrument.

Contacts,  registration, 1350 members, turnover, installed-stock and 95%member-manufacturing boilerplate are low-priority organisational description; employment is repeated centrally and inventoried. No claim about exact membership is admitted as checked.

2026 sales 400000, totalmarket 700000 and 57%are explicitly forecasts;400000/700000=57.14%is internally consistent. No realised-year finding. Assertions about what the bill suggests to consumers and desired 75 euroceiling are judgments/preferences.

Possible future crisis-price reversal,  future investment delay and expected strong effects only in 2030 s are forecasts without falsifiable realised outcome. Claims about GModG constitutionality are conditional policy arguments,  not an asserted judicial holding. Future ETS 2 effects are not errors.
Electricity-tax policy recommendations and claims of future attractiveness are proposals. Exact coalition attribution retained separately unresolved. Boilerplate/contact matter excluded.
Industry resilience,  key technologies and need for greater competitiveness protection are broad evaluative policy framing. The concrete legal/tax premises are inventoried.

Labels untauglich, unbelastbar, nichtpraxistauglich and benchmark suitability conclusions are evaluations of methods; underlying formula, scopeandgaspremises separately checked. Desired benchmark and compensation reforms are preferences.

Whether small waste quantities make pricing proportionate or a rump BEHG useful is a policy judgment. Conditional future scope was checked as proposal/law description,  not guaranteed enacted future coverage.

Predicted 2027 excessdemand, procurementrisk, consumerpass-through magnitude and 500 million euro cost are prospective scenarios. The 500 million corresponds to 100 million premium certificates×5 euros if fully passed through,  but no volume/contract model is disclosed; it is not treated as a factual error. Unavoidable causal pass-through is separately inventoried because of its universal premise. Policy demands and company contacts excluded.

Estimated climate effects of a changedprice, incentive harm, investmentconfidence and required compensating policy are forecasts/judgments. The 4 billion counterfactual methodology and projectionprice assumptions are separately inventoried,  avoiding treatment of predictions as realised facts.

Deutschlandticket being too expensive,  preference for targeted subsidies and social climate dividend,  and prospective opportunities of Social Climate Fund are normative or conditional. Footnotes 7–9 support recommendations rather than an additional numerical assertion. Contact and register boilerplate excluded.
